name: At-Taḥrīm
revelation_details: Madinan (Revealed around 7-8 AH, addressing household dynamics, domestic harmony, privacy, and accountability within the Prophet's family)
core_theme: Defining the boundaries of halal and haram, maintaining domestic integrity without compromising divine law, individual responsibility regardless of family lineage, and contrasting exemplary believing women with rebellious wives of past prophets.
name_origin:
The Surah gets its name, At-Tahrim ("The Prohibition"), directly from its opening verse where Allah gently corrects the Prophet (pbuh) for making something lawful forbidden upon himself to appease his wives:

• "O Prophet, why do you prohibit [yourself from] what Allah has made lawful to you, seeking the approval of your wives? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful."* (Verse 1)

The Incident of Honey

In an authentic report recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (Hadith 5267) and Sahih Muslim (Hadith 1474), Aisha (ra) narrated the primary cause of revelation (Asbab an-Nuzul):

• "The Messenger of Allah (pbuh) used to drink honey at the house of Zainab bint Jahsh (ra) and stay with her. Aisha (ra) and Hafsah (ra) agreed that whichever of them the Prophet (pbuh) visited first, she would say: 'I smell Maghafeer (a sweet but pungent tree gum) on you. Have you eaten Maghafeer?'

• When the Prophet (pbuh) visited one of them and was told this, he disliked smelling of bad odors and replied: 'No, but I drank honey at the house of Zainab bint Jahsh, and I will never drink it again; I have sworn an oath to that. Do not inform anyone of this.'"

Allah revealed the opening verses to establish a vital principle: no human, not even the Prophet (pbuh), has the authority to make forbidden (haram) what Allah has made permissible (halal), even out of extreme kindness or to maintain domestic peace.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: The Incident of Prohibition, Domestic Sensitivity, and Divine Disclosure

points.label: Correction of Excessive Self-Deprivation
points.detail: Allah directly addresses the Prophet (pbuh), asking why he made forbidden (Tahrim) upon himself something pure and lawful that Allah had made permissible, purely to seek the pleasure and peace of his wives. Allah reminds him that He is the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

points.label: The Expiation of Oaths
points.detail: Allah informs the Prophet (pbuh) and the Muslim community that He has already sanctioned a legal mechanism to dissolve oaths (Tahillat Aymanikum) that restrict lawful matters or lead to harm. Allah is the Ultimate Master (Mawla), All-Knowing, and All-Wise.

points.label: The Breach of Confidentiality
points.detail: The Prophet (pbuh) entrusted a confidential matter (a secret) to one of his wives (Hafsa, may Allah be pleased with her). However, she disclosed it to another wife (Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her), and Allah informed His Messenger (pbuh) of this breach.

points.label: Tactful Confrontation
points.detail: When confronting her, the Prophet (pbuh) disclosed only a portion of what he knew out of kindness and dignity, omitting the rest to avoid unnecessary shame. Surprised, she asked, "Who informed you of this?" He replied, "I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware (Al-'Aleem Al-Khabeer).

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
The Surah begins by addressing a delicate domestic trial within the household of the Prophet Muhammad (pbuh), establishing fundamental principles about divine law, marital relations, and oath-taking:
• Correction of Excessive Self-Deprivation: Allah directly addresses the Prophet (pbuh), asking why he made forbidden (Tahrim) upon himself something pure and lawful that Allah had made permissible, purely to seek the pleasure and peace of his wives. Allah reminds him that He is the Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.
• The Expiation of Oaths: Allah informs the Prophet (pbuh) and the Muslim community that He has already sanctioned a legal mechanism to dissolve oaths (Tahillat Aymanikum) that restrict lawful matters or lead to harm. Allah is the Ultimate Master (Mawla), All-Knowing, and All-Wise.
• The Breach of Confidentiality: The Prophet (pbuh) entrusted a confidential matter (a secret) to one of his wives (Hafsa, may Allah be pleased with her). However, she disclosed it to another wife (Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her), and Allah informed His Messenger (pbuh) of this breach.
• Tactful Confrontation: When confronting her, the Prophet (pbuh) disclosed only a portion of what he knew out of kindness and dignity, omitting the rest to avoid unnecessary shame. Surprised, she asked, "Who informed you of this?" He replied, "I was informed by the All-Knowing, the All-Aware (Al-'Aleem Al-Khabeer).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
These opening verses establish that no human - not even the Prophet (pbuh) - has the authority to declare forbidden (Haram) what Allah has made permissible (Halal). Out of intense love and a desire to appease his household, the Prophet (pbuh) attempted to make a personal sacrifice by renouncing a lawful pleasure. Allah immediately corrected this to protect the boundaries of Islamic law: pleasing people must never come at the expense of altering God's permissive boundaries.
Furthermore, this passage offers a masterclass in domestic ethics and emotional intelligence. When the secret was leaked, the Prophet (pbuh) did not react with explosive anger. Instead, he made known part of the issue and ignored part ('Arafa ba'dahu wa 'a'rada 'an ba'd). True nobility in personal relationships involves setting boundaries without rubbing every minor flaw in someone's face. Lastly, the wife's realization that God Himself informed the Messenger served as a reminder that privacy is never truly hidden from Allah - He is Al-'Aleem (the All-Knowing) and Al-Khabeer (the All-Aware).

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Call to Repentance, Marital Harmony, and the Divine Warning to the Wives

points.label: An Invitation to Sincere Repentance
points.detail: Allah commands both wives (Hafsa and Aisha) to turn to Him in repentance, explicitly stating that their hearts had strayed or inclined away from complete propriety (Saghāt Qulūbukumā).

points.label: A Warning Against Collusion
points.detail: Allah warns them that if they cooperate or conspire against the Prophet (pbuh), they must realize his invincible support network: Allah Himself is his Guardian (Mawla), along with the Archangel Gabriel (Jibril), the righteous among the believers, and angels who back him continuously.

points.label: The Divine Standard for Marital Alignment
points.detail: Allah warns that if the Prophet (pbuh) were to divorce them, his Lord could easily replace them with wives who are better in spiritual character:

points.label: Muslimat
points.detail: Submissive to God's will.

points.label: Mu'minat
points.detail: True believers in heart.

points.label: Qanitat
points.detail: Devoutly obedient and humble.

points.label: Ta'ibat
points.detail: Continuously turning back in repentance.

points.label: Abidat
points.detail: Dedicated worshippers.

points.label: Sa'ihat
points.detail: Devoted to fasting/spiritual travel.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah directly addresses the two wives involved in the incident, issuing a firm yet merciful call to self-correction, while outlining the true spiritual standards of marriage:
• An Invitation to Sincere Repentance: Allah commands both wives (Hafsa and Aisha) to turn to Him in repentance, explicitly stating that their hearts had strayed or inclined away from complete propriety (Saghāt Qulūbukumā).
• A Warning Against Collusion: Allah warns them that if they cooperate or conspire against the Prophet (pbuh), they must realize his invincible support network: Allah Himself is his Guardian (Mawla), along with the Archangel Gabriel (Jibril), the righteous among the believers, and angels who back him continuously.
• The Divine Standard for Marital Alignment: Allah warns that if the Prophet (pbuh) were to divorce them, his Lord could easily replace them with wives who are better in spiritual character:
• Muslimat: Submissive to God's will.
• Mu'minat: True believers in heart.
• Qanitat: Devoutly obedient and humble.
• Ta'ibat: Continuously turning back in repentance.
• 'Abidat: Dedicated worshippers.
• Sa'ihat: Devoted to fasting/spiritual travel.
• Comprising both previously married women (Thayyibat) and virgins (Abkara).
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
This passage highlights that proximity to greatness does not grant immunity from accountability. Even the most honored women of the Ummah - the Mothers of the Believers (Ummahat al-Mu'mineen) - were held to exacting standards because of their status. The Quran addresses the root of domestic discord: the condition of the heart (Saghāt Qulūbukumā). Petty jealousy or small domestic maneuvers can imperceptibly veer the heart off-track, requiring swift repentance (Tawbah).
The warning in Verse 5 defines the qualities of an ideal partner in Islam. Notice that physical appearance, wealth, or worldly status are completely absent from this list. Instead, divine success in marriage is anchored in spiritual virtues: repentance, devotion, humility, and active worship. It serves as a reminder to every believer that real honor is gained through spiritual character rather than titles or privilege.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Guarding the Family, the Unyielding Reality of Hell, and Authentic Repentance

points.label: The Responsibility of Home Leadership
points.detail: Believers are commanded: "O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones.

points.label: The Nature of the Guardians of Hell
points.detail: Over this Fire are angels who are stern, rigorous, and severe (Ghiladhun Shidad). They never disobey any command Allah gives them and execute every order precisely.

points.label: The End of Excuses on Judgment Day
points.detail: Disbelievers will be addressed on the Day of Resurrection: "O you who disbelieved, make no excuses today! You are only being recompensed for what you used to do.

points.label: Expiation
points.detail: Allah will wipe away their misdeeds and sins.

points.label: Paradise
points.detail: Admission into Gardens beneath which rivers flow.

points.label: Honor on Judgment Day
points.detail: Allah will not disgrace or humiliate the Prophet (pbuh) and those who believed with him.

points.label: The Radiating Light (Nur)
points.detail: Their light will proceed before them and on their right as they cross into eternity, praying: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us! Indeed, You are over all things competent.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
The Surah expands its focus from the Prophet's household to all believing households, emphasizing domestic leadership, accountability, and the path to ultimate salvation:
• The Responsibility of Home Leadership: Believers are commanded: "O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones."
• The Nature of the Guardians of Hell: Over this Fire are angels who are stern, rigorous, and severe (Ghiladhun Shidad). They never disobey any command Allah gives them and execute every order precisely.
• The End of Excuses on Judgment Day: Disbelievers will be addressed on the Day of Resurrection: "O you who disbelieved, make no excuses today! You are only being recompensed for what you used to do."
• The Path of True Repentance (Tawbatan Nasuha): Believers are called to repent to Allah with sincere, unadulterated repentance (Tawbatan Nasūḥā).
• The Rewards of Sincere Repentance:
 1. Expiation: Allah will wipe away their misdeeds and sins.
 2. Paradise: Admission into Gardens beneath which rivers flow.
 3. Honor on Judgment Day: Allah will not disgrace or humiliate the Prophet (pbuh) and those who believed with him.
 4. The Radiating Light (Nur): Their light will proceed before them and on their right as they cross into eternity, praying: "Our Lord, perfect for us our light and forgive us! Indeed, You are over all things competent.
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
Verse 6 imposes a profound duty on every head of a household. Faith is not merely an individual matter; providing for your family's material needs while neglecting their spiritual wellbeing is a grave oversight. We are commanded to build spiritual defensive walls around our homes to protect our loved ones from destruction. The description of Hell's fuel - "people and stones" - starkly illustrates the outcome of unchecked heedlessness.
In contrast, Verse 8 presents the remedy: Tawbatan Nasuha (sincere repentance). Scholars describe sincere repentance as leaving the sin, regretting it deeply, and resolving never to return to it. The reward for this sincerity is breathtaking: on a Day when millions will be exposed and humiliated, the sincere believers will walk with a light radiating ahead of them. Their humble prayer - "Our Lord, perfect for us our light" - shows that even in the Afterlife, the righteous continuously seek completeness and forgiveness from Allah.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Striving Against Resistance and Historical Warnings of Betrayal

points.label: Command to Strive
points.detail: Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh) to strive (Jahid) against the open disbelievers (Kuffar) and the covert hypocrites (Munafiqeen), remaining firm and unyielding with them. Their ultimate abode is Hell, a miserable destination.

points.label: The Historical Paradigm of Disbelief
points.detail: Allah presents a divine lesson for those who disbelieve through the examples of two women: the wife of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and the wife of Prophet Lut (Lot).

points.label: The Reality of Their Betrayal
points.detail: Both women were married to righteous, chosen servants of Allah, living under the same roof with Prophets of God. Yet, they betrayed their husbands in faith (by siding with the disbelieving elite and mocking the divine message).

points.label: Individual Accountability
points.detail: Their marriage to noble Prophets was of no avail to them against Allah's judgment. On the Day of Judgment, it will be said to them: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter!

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh) to stand firm against external opposition and provides two historical case studies proving that personal connections cannot replace individual faith:
• Command to Strive: Allah commands the Prophet (pbuh) to strive (Jahid) against the open disbelievers (Kuffar) and the covert hypocrites (Munafiqeen), remaining firm and unyielding with them. Their ultimate abode is Hell, a miserable destination.
• The Historical Paradigm of Disbelief: Allah presents a divine lesson for those who disbelieve through the examples of two women: the wife of Prophet Nuh (Noah) and the wife of Prophet Lut (Lot).
• The Reality of Their Betrayal: Both women were married to righteous, chosen servants of Allah, living under the same roof with Prophets of God. Yet, they betrayed their husbands in faith (by siding with the disbelieving elite and mocking the divine message).
• Individual Accountability: Their marriage to noble Prophets was of no avail to them against Allah's judgment. On the Day of Judgment, it will be said to them: "Enter the Fire along with those who enter!
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The transition in Verse 9 from domestic matters to striving (Jihad) highlights that maintaining truth requires both internal discipline and external firmness. But it is Verse 10 that delivers one of the most sobering theological lessons in the Quran: salvation cannot be inherited or transferred through lineage or marriage.
The wives of Nuh and Lut had the ultimate spiritual environment - they ate, slept, and lived alongside two of the greatest Prophets in human history. Yet, because their hearts rejected faith, their husbands' righteousness could not shield them from God's justice. This dismantles all forms of spiritual laziness or false security. Standing before God is entirely individual; no holy spouse, pious parent, or honorable family name can save a person who chooses spiritual hypocrisy.

verse_breakdowns.section_title: Spiritual Archetypes of Faith: Asiya and Maryam

points.label: The First Exemplar - Asiya (The Wife of Pharaoh)
points.detail: Allah sets forth an example for the believers in the wife of Pharaoh. Living under the roof of history's greatest tyrant, she made a immortal prayer:

points.label: The Second Exemplar - Maryam (The Daughter of 'Imran)
points.detail: Allah presents Maryam, who guarded her chastity with absolute purity.

points.label: Divine Conception & Revelation
points.detail: Allah breathed into her through His Angel [Gabriel], and she validated and believed in the words of her Lord and His revealed Scriptures.

points.label: The Quality of Devotion
points.detail: She was recorded among the Qaniteen - those who are deeply, continuously, and humbly obedient to Allah.

verse_breakdowns.content_markdown:
The Surah concludes by presenting two extraordinary women as eternal role models of faith, courage, and spiritual purity for all believers - men and women alike:
• The First Exemplar - Asiya (The Wife of Pharaoh): Allah sets forth an example for the believers in the wife of Pharaoh. Living under the roof of history's greatest tyrant, she made a immortal prayer:
 "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise, and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds, and save me from the wrongdoing people."
• The Second Exemplar - Maryam (The Daughter of 'Imran): Allah presents Maryam, who guarded her chastity with absolute purity.
• Divine Conception & Revelation: Allah breathed into her through His Angel [Gabriel], and she validated and believed in the words of her Lord and His revealed Scriptures.
• The Quality of Devotion: She was recorded among the Qaniteen - those who are deeply, continuously, and humbly obedient to Allah.
verse_breakdowns.reflection:
The ending of Surah At-Tahrim provides a balance to the previous section. Just as the wives of Nuh and Lut proved that a holy environment cannot save a corrupt heart, Asiya (the wife of Pharaoh) proves that a toxic, oppressive environment cannot ruin a pure heart.
Asiya lived in the palace of a man who claimed to be God, yet she maintained unwavering faith. Notice the sequence in her prayer: "Build for me near You a house in Paradise." She prioritized closeness to Allah ('Indaka) before she even asked for the house in Paradise. She was willing to give up a worldly royal palace for closeness to God.
Maryam (may Allah be pleased with her) represents the peak of personal purity, trust in God's word, and devotion (Qunoot). She accepted a miraculous trial with complete faith in Allah's decree. By concluding the Surah with these two women, Allah establishes them not merely as role models for women, but as universal spiritual beacons for all believers - demonstrating that true victory lies in unwavering faith, moral purity, and seeking proximity to Allah above all else.

deep_dives.title: Secrets, Domestic Friction, and Hadith Context
deep_dives.content:
The Surah details the delicate balance of leadership, jealousy, and confidentiality inside a household.

The Breach of Confidentiality

When the Prophet (pbuh) confided a secret to one of his wives (Hafsah, ra) and asked her not to disclose it, she shared it with another wife (Aisha, ra). Allah informed the Prophet (pbuh) of this breach. When he gently brought up part of the conversation with Hafsah (ra), she asked in surprise: "Who informed you of this?" He replied: "I was informed by the Knowing, the Acquainted." (Verse 3).

The Inquiry of Umar ibn Al-Khattab (ra)

This domestic conflict escalated to a point where rumors spread through Madinah that the Prophet (pbuh) was divorcing his wives.

In a narration recorded in Sahih al-Bukhari (Hadith 4913), Abdullah ibn Abbas (ra) asked Umar ibn Al-Khattab (ra) about the two wives mentioned in Verse 4 ("If you two [wives] repent to Allah, [it is best], for your hearts have deviated..."):

• Umar (ra) replied: "I am amazed at your question, O Ibn Abbas! They were Aisha and Hafsah."

• Umar (ra) then related how he had rushed to the Prophet's mosque and found the companions weeping. He sought permission to enter upon the Prophet (pbuh) in his small upper room. He found the Prophet (pbuh) lying on a reed mat that left marks on his side. Umar (ra) cheered the Prophet (pbuh) up and asked: "Have you divorced your wives?" The Prophet (pbuh) lifted his head and said: "No." Umar (ra) shouted: "Allah is the Greatest!

deep_dives.title: The Mandate of Household Protection (Verse 6)
deep_dives.content:
Amidst these personal domestic narratives, Allah addresses every head of a household with a profound command regarding family responsibility:

• "O you who have believed, protect yourselves and your families from a Fire whose fuel is people and stones, over which are [appointed] angels, harsh and severe..."* (Verse 6)

The Spiritual Lesson

Faith is not merely an individual endeavor. A leader of a home cannot be content with their own personal worship while leaving their spouse or children in spiritual neglect. Ali ibn Abi Talib (ra) explained this verse as: "Teach yourselves and your families goodness, and discipline them.

deep_dives.title: Four Women, Four Destinies: The Contrast (Verses 10-12)
deep_dives.content:
The Surah concludes with a masterclass in individual accountability, breaking tribal and marital assumptions by presenting two negative role models and two positive role models among women.

Two Negative Role Models: Personal Choice Over Lineage (Verse 10)

• The Wife of Noah (as) and the Wife of Lot (as): Both women were married to righteous Prophets of God and shared their homes, meals, and lives. Yet, they betrayed their husbands in faith (by aiding the corrupt societies around them).
• The Lesson: Being closely tied or married to a righteous scholar, leader, or Prophet will not save anyone on the Day of Judgment if their own heart lacks sincere faith.

Two Positive Role Models: Faith Triumphing Over Circumstance (Verses 11-12)

• Asiya, the Wife of Pharaoh (Verse 11): She lived in the house of the greatest tyrant on earth, surrounded by luxury, power, and disbelief. Yet, she secretly held firm to faith and prayed: "My Lord, build for me near You a house in Paradise and save me from Pharaoh and his deeds..."
• Maryam, the Daughter of 'Imran (Verse 12): She guarded her chastity, believed in the words of her Lord and His scriptures, and was entirely devoted in obedience, serving as a beacon of purity and courage.

The Surah closes by demonstrating that spiritual destiny is an individual choice: no bad environment can corrupt a soul truly connected to God (like Asiya), and no holy environment can save a rebellious heart (like the wives of Noah and Lot).
